Wilderness  Plan Public  Hearing  Principal Planner Bowcock reported on the Wilderness Plan along with a
  power point presentation. She stated that in 2006, the City acquired 208 acres
  in north La Verne through State grant funds obtained in cooperation with the
  County of Los Angeles, the Trust for Public Land, and the La Verne Land
  Conservancy. This land was combined with 150 acres already owned by the
  City to create an open space preserve of 358 acres, collectively referred to as
  the Wilderness Area. The Wilderness Area Management and Public Access
  Plan includes selective habitat enhancement actions, the resolution of public
  safety hazards, and opportunities for limited controlled public access as part of
  the City' s stewardship responsibilities for the Wilderness Area. The
  Management Plan includes goals for specific physical improvements or
  management policies that would implement the vision for the Wilderness Area.
  She stated that there are two phases being proposed. Phase 1 consists of
  maintenance, security, fuel modification, planting, and protecting the
  wilderness area. Phase 2 includes the development of the loop trails and the
  increase of public access to the area. Conditions were also added that if there
  is ever a desire for Phase 2 to move forward, an update to the Environmental
  Impact Report ( as necessary), a public workshop, and City Council approval
  would be required prior to implementation. This will ensure that Phase 2 will
  only move forward with proper noti cation to the residents and ultimately a
  vote of the City Council. Staff and the Planning Commission recommend City
  Council adopt Resolution Number 22- 72, approving the Wilderness Area
  Management and Public Access Plan and certifying the Final Environmental
  Impact Report.

  Mayor Hepburn opened the public hearing and called for public comment on
  this matter.

  Several residents expressed their concerns and objections to the proposed
  loop trail and increased public access, fire hazard, homeless living in the area,
  and public  safety. ( To hear what was said during  public comment, please visit
  the City' s website to view the archived Council meeting.)

  Special Counsel Barbara Leibold stated that the Wilderness Conservation
  grant terms requires that the wilderness area be managed for the purpose of
  wildlife habitat preservation and other conditions

  It was moved by Crosby and seconded by Kashifalghita, and unanimously
  carried to adopt Resolution Number 22- 72, approving the Wilderness Area
  Management and Public Access Plan and certifying the Final Environmental
  Impact Report.

14.  Adjournment at 9: 30 p. m. in memory of retired Water Superintendent Charlie Farrell. Charlie was employed with
  the City of La Verne for 35 years.  Charlie was born and raised in Brooklyn, New York and joined the United
  States Air Force stationed  in Boise, Idaho.  After his service, he moved to La Verne and started his career with
  the City of La Verne in the Parks Department and later transferred to the Water Department and became
  Water/Sewer Superintendent. His commitment to the La Verne community persisted through his retirement as he
  volunteered for the La Verne Fire Department, Fourth of July parade, and Christmas Candy Giveaways for years.
  Additionally, Charlie fostered youth development with the local Boy Scouts and Booster Club groups. Charlie was
  honored with the Pride of La Verne Award in 2006 in recognition of his dedication and passion for the La Verne
  community.  He is survived by 3 children, 2 stepchildren and he was Papa to 12 grandchildren and 7 great
  grandchildren;  and
